rubric:
1. Multi-head attention gives every query head its own key and value, so the cache stores two full sets of heads (keys and values) per token per layer. It is the quality reference and the largest cache.
2. Multi-query attention shares a single key head and a single value head across all query heads. The cache shrinks to one head pair, and that extreme sharing is where quality usually drops.
3. Grouped-query attention clusters query heads into groups and stores one key/value head per group, so the cache sits between the two extremes. Describes it as the compromise when one shared head is too lossy.
4. Multi-head latent attention jointly compresses keys and values into a low-rank latent and caches that latent, then reconstructs per-head keys and values. The cache scales with the latent width, and query heads are not forced to share one key/value vector.
5. Ties the choice to decode cost: the cache grows with layers, sequence length, and batch, and it is read on every new token. Picks multi-head when the cache fits, grouped-query or multi-query when bandwidth dominates, and the latent form when a small cache is required without collapsing to one shared head.
